fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), tells his soul, "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds…" (Psalm 103:2). I once searched the whole bakery for my chef's hat while it was sitting on my head. If a stamper can lose track of what's right on top of him, a soul can lose track of kind deeds. So David keeps them in front of his soul.

Good guess, but no enemies show up in this verse. David's soul gets two instructions here: "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all His kind deeds…" The whole focus is on what the LORD has done.

Waiting is a real thing, and I did plenty of it in the back of a junk drawer. But David doesn't mention it in this verse. What he tells his soul is, "…do not forget all His kind deeds…" He's pointing it back at what the LORD has already done.

You got it. The LORD "…satisfies you with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s." (Psalm 103:5). David picks an eagle for his picture. Renewed means made fresh again, and I know a little about that, since I went from a junk drawer to a bakery.

Priests are a fair thought, but David doesn't name them in this verse. What he says is, "The LORD executes righteousness and justice for all the oppressed." The verse says ALL the oppressed, so it's a wide group.

True, baker. David says, "He made known His ways to Moses, His deeds to the people of Israel." (Psalm 103:7). So the LORD made His ways known to Moses. And He made His deeds known to the people of Israel.

That's not what the verse says, friend. David says, "He made known His ways to Moses, His deeds to the people of Israel." (Psalm 103:7). So the LORD made His ways known to Moses. And He made His deeds known to the people of Israel.

That's right. David says, "For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His loving devotion for those who fear Him." (Psalm 103:11). David compares how great His loving devotion is to how high the heavens are above the earth. And it's for those who fear Him.

That's right, baker. David says, "But from everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him…" (Psalm 103:17). Notice that little word BUT. The flower vanishes when the wind passes over it (Psalm 103:16), and the LORD's loving devotion doesn't end. That's good news.

Good thought, since David just said a person's days are like grass and like a flower that vanishes. But he sets the LORD's loving devotion against that. The verse says it extends "…from everlasting to everlasting…" It goes well past a lifetime.

The verse says otherwise, baker. David says the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him, "…and His righteousness to their children’s children…" (Psalm 103:17). So the answer is True: His righteousness goes on to their children's children. Children's children! I get nervous handing one tray across the counter, and this keeps going down the line.

Yes, baker. David says, "As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear Him." (Psalm 103:13). That's a dad looking after his children. I have six little cookie cutter kids, so this one lands close to home.
Zion is a natural guess. But David doesn't narrow it down to any one place. He says, "…His kingdom rules over all." That's a lot bigger than one spot on the map.
Judah is a natural guess. But David doesn't stop there. The verse says, "…His kingdom rules over all." His throne is in heaven, and His rule reaches everything.

Kings are an understandable guess. But the verse names someone else. It says, "Bless the LORD, all His angels mighty in strength who carry out His word…" Those are the ones David calls on in verse 20.

Elders would make sense for a psalm, but they aren't in this verse. David calls on "…all His angels mighty in strength who carry out His word, who hearken to the voice of His command." That's a crew that listens close, and I can barely hear my own oven timer. These are the ones who carry out His word.
